observed_mechanics: 0x004ad559 MOV dword ptr [EBP-0xb0],ECX then 0x004ad56f MOV EAX,[EBP-0xb0]: the receiver is spilled once and reloaded at each of five separate use sites

0x004ad55f/0x004ad562 and 0x004ad567/0x004ad56a: the SAME address [EBP-0x1c] is passed to 0x00409c00 twice. The second call is redundant in the observed build, since 0x00409c00 writes six fixed constants. This is preserved in the reconstruction rather than collapsed.
0x004ad575 ADD EAX,0x18 with EAX = the receiver: the rigblock vector is the receiver's +0x18, and its end pointer is its +0x1c
0x004ad58a MOV EAX,[ECX+0x4] / 0x004ad58d SUB EAX,[EDX] / 0x004ad58f SAR EAX,0x2: the count is the byte difference shifted arithmetically right by 2, i.e. four bytes per element

0x004ad595 CMP dword ptr [EBP-0x4],0x0 / 0x004ad599 JBE 0x004ad6d8: an UNSIGNED less-or-equal against zero, so a count of exactly 0 skips the whole body and a negative count (which SAR can produce) does not, since its unsigned value is large

0x004ad5c1/0x004ad5c3/0x004ad5c5/0x004ad5ca/0x004ad5cb with ECX = *(this+0x18): the bounds port is called as (rigblock, &[EBP-0x3c], 0, 0, 0). The three literal zeros are the mode and the two flag arguments; 0x0044ae00's own decompiled body confirms that parameter order.

0x004ad5d6 stores the port's return value, and 0x004ad5e2 ADD EAX,0xc followed by 0x004ad5e8/0x004ad5ec/0x004ad5f2 copies floats 3, 4 and 5 to [EBP-0x10] while 0x004ad600/0x004ad603/0x004ad60c copies floats 0, 1 and 2 to [EBP-0x1c]. [EBP-0x10] is exactly [EBP-0x1c] + 0xc, so the two halves together fill one contiguous 24-byte object: this is a whole-BoundingBox copy, interleaved by the compiler.
0x004ad5f8..0x004ad60c therefore OVERWRITE the accumulator rather than merging into it, so element 0 seeds the result and is not unioned
0x004ad60f MOV dword ptr [EBP-0x24],0x1: the loop index starts at 1, not 0, because element 0 was consumed by the seed block
0x004ad616/0x004ad61c/0x004ad625/0x004ad62b/0x004ad631/0x004ad634/0x004ad636: the count is recomputed from this+0x18 inside the loop preamble and stored to [EBP-0x20]; it is not hoisted
0x004ad63c JMP 0x004ad647: the loop is a do-while shape - the increment block at 0x004ad63e is placed before the test and reached by a backward jump from the end of the body at 0x004ad6d3

0x004ad647/0x004ad64a/0x004ad64d: MOV ECX,index / CMP ECX,count / JGE tail. JGE is a SIGNED comparison, so a negative count produced by the arithmetic shift makes the loop exit immediately - which is the opposite of what the unsigned JBE at 0x004ad599 would do for the same value. The two comparisons disagree for negative counts; this is recorded rather than reconciled.
0x004ad653 MOVZX EDX,byte ptr [EBP+0xc] / 0x004ad657 TEST EDX,EDX / 0x004ad659 JZ 0x004ad692: when the flag byte is zero the filter is skipped entirely and every element is processed
0x004ad661..0x004ad67e: with the flag set, element[index] is re-derived from this+0x18 and passed to 0x00435d40 in ECX

0x004ad689 MOVZX EAX,AL / 0x004ad68c TEST EAX,EAX / 0x004ad68e JNZ 0x004ad692 / 0x004ad690 JMP 0x004ad63e: a false predicate advances the index WITHOUT touching the accumulator, and the FST-style double test means only the low byte of the predicate's return is examined
0x004ad692..0x004ad6c5: the second bounds-port call, writing to [EBP-0x54] this time, again with the three literal zeros
0x004ad6ca PUSH EAX / 0x004ad6cb LEA ECX,[EBP-0x1c] / 0x004ad6ce CALL 0x0043f050: the union, with the accumulator as the thiscall receiver and the freshly produced box as the single stack argument

0x004ad6d8 LEA EDX,[EBP-0x1c] / 0x004ad6db PUSH EDX / 0x004ad6dc MOV ECX,[EBP+0x8] / 0x004ad6df CALL 0x00511140: the final 24-byte store into the caller's out parameter, reached both from the count==0 shortcut and from the loop exit
0x004ad6e4 MOV EAX,[EBP+0x8] / 0x004ad6ea RET 0x8: the out parameter is returned and the callee pops both stack arguments

0x00409c00's body stores 0x7f7fffff into words 0, 1, 2 and 0xff7fffff into words 3, 4, 5, i.e. +FLT_MAX into the lower corner and -FLT_MAX into the upper corner. That is an INVERTED, not a zero, box, and it is what makes 0x0043f050's emptiness test work.

0x0043f050's body is `if (a.lower[0] <= a.upper[0]) { componentwise min/max merge } else { a = b }`, pairing element 0 with 3, 1 with 4 and 2 with 5. That is a BoundingBox union with an emptiness branch, and it fixes the six-float layout as lower={0,1,2}, upper={3,4,5}.
0x00511140's body copies exactly six dwords from src to dst and returns dst

0x00435d40's body walks param_1 = *(param_1 + 0x33c) for at most 100 iterations, breaking with a 1 when bits 0x80 or 0x100 of [param_1+0xdc8] or bit 0x8 of [param_1+0xdcc] are set, and returning 0 when the chain ends or the pointer is null. It is an ancestor-chain flag test, not a local one.

control_flow.count_signedness_conflict: 0x004ad599 uses an unsigned comparison and 0x004ad64d a signed one on values produced by the same arithmetic shift. For a count of 0 the unsigned test fires and the body is skipped. For a negative count - which a SAR can produce if end precedes begin - the unsigned test does NOT fire while the signed loop test DOES exit at once, so the observable effect is: the seed block runs, then the loop body never runs, and element 0's box is the result. This is recorded from the listing; no attempt is made to decide whether it is intended.

semantic_contract: Non-virtual member of a model-state object, ECX receiver, two callee-cleaned stack arguments, and the first argument returned unchanged in EAX. The contract is 'compute the aggregate local-space bounding box of my rigblock list and write it to the caller's box'. Invariants, in order: (1) a 24-byte accumulator is set to the inverted empty-box sentinel, lower = +FLT_MAX and upper = -FLT_MAX, and it is set twice, redundantly; (2) the element count is (end - begin) >> 2 over the vector at receiver+0x18, and a count of zero short-circuits straight to the store, so an empty rigblock list produces an EMPTY box rather than a zero box; (3) element 0's bounds, computed with mode 0 and both flags clear, OVERWRITE the accumulator - it seeds the result and is never unioned, and it is not subject to the filter flag; (4) elements 1..count-1 are folded in with a BoundingBox union that replaces the accumulator when the accumulator is still the empty sentinel and otherwise expands it componentwise; (5) when the filter flag byte is non-zero, an element is folded in only if an ancestor-chain walk of at most 100 levels, through the parent pointer at +0x33c, finds flag bit 0x80 or 0x100 at +0xdc8 or bit 0x8 at +0xdcc on the element or on any ancestor - so a clean rigblock under a flagged ancestor is excluded, and a zero flag disables the test entirely; (6) the accumulator is copied to the caller's box and the caller's box pointer is returned. The receiver is only read; no field of it is written.
classification_rationale: The behaviour is fully determined and heavily corroborated: all 112 instructions are read, all five callees are resolved to concrete operations from their own decompiled bodies rather than from their names, the 24-byte payload layout is confirmed three independent ways (0x00409c00's six constants, 0x0043f050's index pairing, 0x00511140's six-dword copy) and matches the SDK's BoundingBox declaration, and the loop's start index, signed/unsigned comparison mix, filter polarity and empty-list behaviour are all read from the listing. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC for one named reason: the owning type is bounded rather than established. The receiver's +0x18 matches the SDK-declared mRigblocks vector and the surrounding code region matches EditorModel, but no vtable exists in the typed program to close the identity, and this binary has no RTTI. That is exactly the material element the batch's BOUNDED_SEMANTIC definition names, and a STRONG_SEMANTIC claim would require a located vtable or runtime evidence, neither of which exists.
semantic_findings: This is an aggregate-bounds computation over a rigblock list, not a store or a query: the whole body is seed-then-union, and the union primitive is read directly out of 0x0043f050's source rather than assumed from its name.

The accumulator is seeded by OVERWRITING with element 0, not by unioning element 0 into the empty sentinel. Both give the same result when element 0 is non-empty, but they differ when element 0 is itself empty, and the body takes the overwrite path unconditionally.

The empty-list case writes the inverted sentinel to the caller's box: lower = +FLT_MAX, upper = -FLT_MAX. Any caller that treats lower <= upper as a valid box will mis-handle that, so this is a real precondition on the caller rather than a neutral default.

The filter flag's sense is inverted from the usual: a ZERO flag means no filtering, a non-zero flag means gate every element from index 1 onward. Element 0 is never gated, so the flag cannot suppress the seed.

The filter predicate is an ancestor-chain test, not a local one. It walks the parent pointer at +0x33c up to 100 levels and can therefore exclude a rigblock because of a flag set on something above it in the hierarchy.
The return value carries no information: it is the out parameter, read back out of [EBP+0x8] at 0x004ad6e4. Callers can and do ignore it, and the one inspected caller does.

The count is computed twice, once before the seed and once in the loop preamble, and the two comparisons guarding it disagree on sign: 0x004ad599 is unsigned and 0x004ad64d is signed. For a well-formed vector both agree; for end < begin the seed still runs and the loop body never does. Recorded from the listing without choosing an interpretation.

The double call to 0x00409c00 on the same address is redundant in the observed build. It is preserved in the reconstruction because removing it would be an unexplained divergence, and flagged as a codegen artefact rather than an invariant.

The 24-byte copy of element 0's box is emitted as two 12-byte halves at interleaved addresses (upper first at [EBP-0x10], then lower at [EBP-0x1c]); reconstructing it as a single block copy would be behaviourally equivalent but not structurally faithful.

The bounds port is always called with mode 0 and both flags clear, so rigblock CHILD bounds are never folded in by this function. Any caller needing a whole-hierarchy bound must get it from the port's own recursive path, which this body never enables.

0x004ad6f0, 0x930 bytes away in the same region, iterates the same +0x18 array and reads the same +0xdc8 flag word, which independently corroborates the field identification - while operating on a different element type, since its elements have a float at +0x4c where this class has a byte.
unresolved_questions: The owning class. The +0x18 vector matches Spore/Editors/EditorModel.h's mRigblocks exactly and the code region matches, but no vtable was located and there is no RTTI, so the class is a candidate and not a claim.
The method name. Nothing in the binary or the SDK names it; the reconstruction's name describes the operation, not a recovered identifier.

What the filter flag byte means to a caller. Observed only as 'non-zero enables the ancestor-chain test'; no caller's intent was established, and the three uninspected callers in the 0x0057/0x0058 region were not disassembled.
Which of the two count comparisons is intended for a malformed vector, and whether a negative count can occur in practice.
Why the accumulator is default-initialised twice.
What the 24-byte box the caller at 0x00586ee8 receives is used for beyond the first float it reads at 0x00586eed; the rest of that caller's use was not followed.
Whether 0x0044ae00 with mode 0 is the right mode for every caller of this function, or whether some caller-visible behaviour depends on the mode this body hard-codes to 0.
The five uninspected call sites at 0x00574bb4, 0x00583e94, 0x0058072b, 0x005addc6 and the pair at 0x005ae348/0x005ae35d.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this function. Static analysis cannot show whether the rigblock vector is ever empty in a live editor session, which is the only path that produces the inverted sentinel in a caller's box.
A trace must record the actual filter-flag values passed by callers, which is the only way to learn whether the ancestor-chain test is ever active in the shipping build.
A trace must confirm that the 100-level ceiling in 0x00435d40 is never reached, i.e. that no rigblock hierarchy in the shipping data is deeper than 100.
A differential test must confirm the box is written even when the list is empty, since that is the invariant a caller is most likely to depend on incorrectly.
